subject: Urgent: rollout causing hot-path latency spike and 5xxs
thread_body:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@trailhead.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Trailhead Analytics SRE <sre@trailhead.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike & 5xxs after v5.2 rollout

Hi Ben —

We started seeing a sharp P95 latency increase (~2.3x) and ~4% 5xx error rate on our inference routes at 08:40 PDT, immediately after the v5.2 model variant + new 8-bit quant profile was pushed for our account. Throughput dropped as well (backlog spiking). This is affecting production recommendation endpoints.

Attached: trailhead_perf_snapshot_20270803.csv (summary + traces).

Can you confirm whether Redwood rolled a global change, or if this was targeted to our Dedicated pool? We need an immediate mitigation path (rollback or toggle).

Thanks,
Megan Ortiz
Head of Platform
Trailhead Analytics

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@trailhead.ai>
Cc: Trailhead Analytics SRE <sre@trailhead.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:27:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike & 5xxs after v5.2 rollout

Megan — thanks for the quick ping and for the snapshot. I’m escalating immediately.

Immediate actions I’ve taken:
- Opened priority SEV and notified on-call infra.
- Temporarily pinned your tenant to v5.1 and disabled the 8-bit quant profile for your Dedicated pool (this should stop further degradation).
- Asking our performance team to analyze KV-cache pressure and kernel selection behavior for the v5.2/8bit path.

I’ll coordinate a short conference call with you and our engineers in 30 minutes. Expect a status update within 20.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:35:45 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Trailhead live incident — need hot-path analysis and exec visibility

Team — forwarding the customer report. Key points:
- Time: 08:40 PDT saw p95 ~2.3x and 4% 5xx; backlog increased; throughput drop.
- Trigger appears to be v5.2 + 8-bit quant profile rollout.
- Customer currently pinned back to v5.1 on our change — mitigation in place but they want a root cause and rollback plan if needed.

Please treat as priority. Evelyn, please join the call with Trailhead. Vivek, can you do an initial triage on model-runner behavior (kv cache miss/eviction, kernel fallback, mem pressure) and check scheduler metrics for their Dedicated pool? Laura, finance/sales side — Trailhead is a mid-enterprise with a reserved capacity deal (TR-4719); flag any SLA credit risk for leadership.

Thanks,
Ben

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:12:07 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Trailhead live incident — need hot-path analysis and exec visibility

Quick triage results:
- Observed increased kernel fallback to slower GEMM path on a subset of nodes serving Trailhead after v5.2 + 8-bit profile. This correlates with higher CPU usage on host side and cache churn.
- Quantized attention kernels introduced a new memory layout that increased per-request KV footprint when sequence lengths exceeded 1k (Trailhead uses long contexts for recommendations).
- Scheduler started batching suboptimally due to higher variance in step time; this amplified p95.
- No underlying node-level hardware failure; it’s algorithmic/shape-related.

Proposed immediate remediation (short term):
1) Keep Trailhead pinned to v5.1 for now (done).
2) Roll a targeted patch that disables the new attention layout for long-seq profiles (we can backport a guard flag). I’ve attached diff-hotfix-5.2.patch for review.
3) Add a temporary config to force legacy batching policy for their pool.

I will continue deeper profile analysis (heap snapshots, kv occupancy) and will produce a mitigation runbook. If engineering agrees, we can attempt a staged re-roll within 24 hours with monitoring hooks.

-Vivek
Sr. Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachments referenced: diff-hotfix-5.2.patch

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@trailhead.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike & 5xxs after v5.2 rollout

Megan — sorry for the disruption. We take incidents like this very seriously. Ben has already pinned you to v5.1 and Vivek has a high-confidence mitigation path.

Next steps for you (short):
- We will perform the targeted patch to disable the new layout for long contexts in a staged manner. Expected window: 4–6 hours for rollout + verification.
- We’ll keep your pool on legacy batching until we revalidate telemetry.
- I’ll send an executive summary and an incident timeline within 6 hours.

Laura — I’ll flag potential SLA impact postmortem to ops leadership. Ben, please keep me looped on any asks from the customer about credits.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@trailhead.ai>, Trailhead Analytics SRE <sre@trailhead.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident update: patch applied to Trailhead pool (v5.2 guard)

Megan —
Quick customer-facing update: Vivek and infra applied the guard patch to the nodes serving your Dedicated pool at 14:50 PDT and enforced the legacy batching policy. Early telemetry shows P95 trending back towards baseline and 5xx rate falling to ~0.2%. No further customer throttles observed.

What we’ll deliver next:
- Incident timeline and root cause analysis (EOD).
- A patch backport and a tested re-roll plan for v5.2 with long-context guard and improved kernel selection heuristics.
- Runbook sections added: emergency rollback (already executed), and a toggle for quant-layout gating.

If you’d like, we can schedule a technical postmortem tomorrow to walk through the changelist and validation steps.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep monitoring.

—Ben

Megan/Evelyn —
Attaching the initial postmortem and runbook: runbook-hotpath-mitigation.md and diff-hotfix-5.2.patch. Summary:
- Root cause: new attention memory layout in v5.2 increased KV footprint for long contexts which triggered suboptimal kernel fallback and batching variance in a subset of nodes.
- Impact: P95 spike up to 2.3x, temporary throughput drop, ~4% 5xx on your production routes between 08:40–09:15 PDT on Aug 3.
- Resolution: guard patch applied; full backport queued for release after validation.

We’ll schedule a re-roll window next week with you and run the validation plan jointly. Laura, please prepare SLA assessment notes for procurement.

Thanks — closing this thread for communication; reopening if anything else crops up.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
